scope.detail: Plus this lane's own artifacts: the manifest, the .ops/sync file and this proof bundle. `packages/db/src/runtime-repositories.ts` is a Tier C EXACT path, which is why this lane is T1 rather than the T3 an earlier draft proposed. No workflow, no merge control, no containment setting, no migration and no deploy path is touched.

limits: This lane changes where team and player search READ from -- the provider `participants` observation layer instead of the empty canonical `teams`/`players` tables -- and not what the published `TeamSearchResult`/`PlayerSearchResult` interfaces promise. No caller signature changes.

It seeds nothing and it deletes nothing. The canonical `teams`, `players` and `player_team_assignments` tables remain empty under parked provider ingestion, deliberately, and every row in `participants` is preserved. The proof-fixture repair is a read filter, never a DELETE; production data deletion is reserved decision 1 and is not proposed.

The proof-fixture exclusion keys on a non-null `metadata.proofIssue`, never on a missing team relationship. Measured read-only against production 2026-09-07 the two predicates select exactly the same 26 rows, so this distinction is invisible in today's data and is asserted against a constructed row instead: a player carrying no marker and no team survives with `teamId: null`.

`getEventBrowse`/`searchBrowse` carry a separate participant-vs-canonical key mismatch. It is real, it is recorded, and it is OUT OF SCOPE here -- those paths are not in this lane's file_scope_lock and are not touched.

The staging receipt proves persistence, non-delivery, and the proof-fixture exclusion/preservation pair on a real database. It does not constitute the Milestone 1 pilot, which requires Griff's own browser against the deployed system.
